exercise.name: Front Plank with Leg Lift

reference.title: Front Plank with Leg Lift (male)
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge

exercise.mechanics: Isometric trunk (anti-extension, anti-rotation) with hip extension

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the leg lifts, breathe in as it lowers; keep the brace on throughout.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 1 s hold, 1 s down per leg

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, 1 s hold, 1 s down
prescription.progression: Longer holds at the top, then the plank with an arm and leg lift

cues.text: Forearm plank: elbows under the shoulders, body in one line from head to heels.
Squeeze the right glute and lift the straight leg a hand-width or two; hips stay level and square.
Hold briefly without arching the low back or rolling the hips.
Lower the toes back to the mat under control.
Same with the left leg: lift from the glute, not from the low back.
Hold the plank briefly, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to get the leg higher
mistakes.fix: Lift only as high as the hips stay level; the movement is at the hip.

mistakes.mistake: Hips rolling toward the lifted leg
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones pointing at the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sagging when one foot is up
mistakes.fix: Brace harder and squeeze the standing-leg glute.
Keep the lifting leg long, toes reaching back.

kinematics.norm: Straight line held throughout; the lift happens at the hip (clinical opinion)
A small lift of about 10-15 degrees past the body line keeps the pelvis level (clinical opinion); unilateral hip extension in a plank raises gluteal activity (Boren 2011)
Level and square, no rotation toward the lifted leg (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, 1 s hold, 1 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low back pain that increases in the plank: shorten the hold or drop to the knee plank.
High blood pressure: breathe steadily; long breath-held efforts raise blood pressure.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: hands together (forearms in a slight V) or an incline plank with the forearms on a bench.
Elbow discomfort: fold the mat under the forearms.
progressions: Front plank with arm and leg lift.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and obliques resist sagging and rotation when one foot leaves the floor; a three-point base raises the trunk demand over a normal plank (clinical opinion; Ekstrom 2007 for the bridge family).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Gluteus maximus extends the lifted hip and holds the standing hip level; hip extension from a plank position gave high gluteal activity in Boren 2011.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Gluteus maximus extends the lifted hip and holds the standing hip level; hip extension from a plank position gave high gluteal activity in Boren 2011.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Obliques stop the pelvis rotating toward the lifted leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Obliques stop the pelvis rotating toward the lifted leg (clinical opinion).
